title: When the noncommutative AM-GM inequality holds
abstract: For arbitrary real positive semidefinite matrices A_i whose sum is at most n I, the uniform average W of ordered products of m distinct matrices satisfies -I <= W <= I when n >= 2 ceil(m/2)^2. When n >= 4m^2 its lower bound improves to -(1-1/(2m)) I. The formalization also proves the stronger lower bound -(1-1/m) I at the quadratic threshold, the original sine-node criterion, and the cubic-size corollary. The statements retain the original arbitrary PSD and sum-at-most-nI hypotheses. Harmonic decomposition, positive root quadratures, matrix Gram factors, normalized coefficient extraction, and the original rounded-node lower-bound proof are constructed in the repository.
